intro_html: Ham and bean soup is the original leftover recipe. Somebody figured out a long time ago that the least valuable part of a ham makes the best pot of soup, and nobody has improved on it since. Diced ham, white beans, tomatoes and the usual carrot, celery and onion base. It carries 32 grams of protein for about $1.93 a bowl.
cost_closing_html: About $1.93 a bowl. If you happen to be working with leftover holiday ham instead of buying it fresh, this recipe gets dramatically cheaper, because the ham is the single biggest line on the list.
shop_smart: Leftover ham is free ham. This recipe exists to use up the end of a holiday roast. If you are buying, watch for whole hams on markdown after a holiday and freeze the diced meat in bags.
Canned white beans skip the overnight soak. Dried beans cost less if you plan ahead, but canned means you can decide to make this at four in the afternoon.
Chicken broth is the second biggest line, so buy the big cartons. Store brand is fine here. Between the ham and the tomatoes, this soup is already well seasoned.
Carrots, celery and onion are the cheap backbone. Buy them whole rather than pre chopped and the entire vegetable base costs less than the ham trimmings.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the onion, carrots and celery, and drain and rinse the white beans.
Heat a large pot and cook the diced ham until the edges brown and it renders a little fat. Browning the ham first is what gives this soup its backbone.
Add the onion, carrots and celery to the pot and cook until they soften and pick up the browned bits.
Stir in the chili powder, dried parsley, black pepper and bay leaves and cook for a minute.
Pour in the chicken broth and the diced tomatoes and bring everything up to a simmer.
Add the drained white beans and simmer gently, mashing a scoop of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the broth naturally.
Pull the bay leaves, taste for salt, and cook the rice separately to serve it under the soup.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and ladle the exact amount over rice in each container, stirring between scoops so the ham and beans stay even. Every bowl lands near 574 calories and 32 grams of protein.

head.keywords: ham and bean soup, white bean soup, leftover ham recipe, cannellini bean soup, budget meal prep
steps: Brown the diced ham in a large pot until the edges color.
Add the diced onion, carrots and celery and cook until softened.
Stir in the chili powder, parsley, black pepper and bay leaves.
Add the chicken broth and diced tomatoes and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the drained white beans, mash some against the pot to thicken, and serve over cooked rice.
